claim: FcγRIIB binding to its ligand suppresses immune cell activation.
source: FcγRIIB binding to its ligand suppresses immune cell activation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established function of FcγRIIB.

claim: A single-nucleotide polymorphic (SNP) change, I232T, in the transmembrane (TM) domain of FcγRIIB loses its suppressive function.
source: A single-nucleotide polymorphic (SNP) change, I232T, in the transmembrane (TM) domain of FcγRIIB loses its suppressive function, which is clinically associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by clinical association data presented in the manuscript.

claim: I232T polymorphism is clinically associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
source: A single-nucleotide polymorphic (SNP) change, I232T, in the transmembrane (TM) domain of FcγRIIB loses its suppressive function, which is clinically associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by epidemiological data and citations in the manuscript.

claim: I232T tilts FcγRIIB's TM domain.
source: Previously, we reported that I232T tilts FcγRIIB's TM domain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references previous work by the authors.

claim: I232T tilting of the TM domain bends the FcγRIIB's ectodomain toward plasma membrane to allosterically impede FcγRIIB's ligand association.
source: In this study, combining with molecular dynamics simulations and single-cell FRET assay, we further reveal that such tilting by I232T unexpectedly bends the FcγRIIB's ectodomain toward plasma membrane to allosterically impede FcγRIIB's ligand association.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by molecular dynamics simulations and FRET assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: I232T substitution reduces in situ two-dimensional binding affinities of FcγRIIB to interact with IgG1 by three to four folds.
source: I232T substitution reduces in situ two-dimensional binding affinities and association rates of FcγRIIB to interact with its ligands, IgG1, IgG2 and IgG3 by three to four folds.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by adhesion frequency assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: I232T substitution reduces in situ two-dimensional binding affinities of FcγRIIB to interact with IgG2 by three to four folds.

claim: FcγRIIB is widely expressed on most types of immune cells including B cells, plasma cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, macrophages, neutrophils, basophils, mast cells and even memory CD8+ T cells.
source: FcγRIIB is widely expressed on most types of immune cells including B cells, plasma cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, macrophages, neutrophils, basophils, mast cells and even memory CD8+ T cells (Starbeck-Miller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Among all the immune-receptors for Fc portion of IgG molecules (FcγRs), FcγRIIB is unique due to its suppressive function against immune cell activation.
source: Among all the immune-receptors for Fc portion of IgG molecules (FcγRs), FcγRIIB is unique due to its suppressive function against immune cell activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the human FcγRIIB gene extensively influence the susceptibility toward autoimmune disorders.
source: It has been shown that single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the human FcγRIIB gene extensively influence the susceptibility toward autoimmune disorders (Kyogoku et al., 2002; Niederer et al., 2010; Smith and Clatworthy, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: A T-to-C variant in exon 5 (rs1050501) of FcγRIIB causes the I232T substitution within the transmembrane domain.
source: A T-to-C variant in exon 5 (rs1050501) of FcγRIIB causes the I232T substitution (FcγRIIB-I232T) within the transmembrane (TM) domain and is positively associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in the homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T populations as reported in epidemiological studies (Chu et al., 2004; Clatworthy et al., 2007; Kyogoku et al., 2002; Niederer et al., 2010; Siriboonrit et al., 2003; Willcocks et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The I232T substitution is positively associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in the homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T populations.
source: A T-to-C variant in exon 5 (rs1050501) of FcγRIIB causes the I232T substitution (FcγRIIB-I232T) within the transmembrane (TM) domain and is positively associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in the homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T populations as reported in epidemiological studies (Chu et al., 2004; Clatworthy et al., 2007; Kyogoku et al., 2002; Niederer et al., 2010; Siriboonrit et al., 2003; Willcocks et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple epidemiological studies.

claim: Monocytes harboring FcγRIIB-232T are hyper-activated with augmented FcγRI-triggered phospholipase D activation and calcium signaling.
source: Previous biochemical studies revealed that monocytes harboring FcγRIIB-232T (232T) are hyper-activated with augmented FcγRI-triggered phospholipase D activation and calcium signaling (Floto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: B lymphocytes expressing 232T are of hyperactivity with abnormal elevation of PLCγ2 activation, proliferation and calcium mobilization.
source: B lymphocytes expressing 232T are of hyperactivity with abnormal elevation of PLCγ2 activation, proliferation and calcium mobilization (Kono et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: 232T-expressing B cells lose the ability to inhibit the oligomerization of B cell receptors (BCRs) upon co-ligation between BCR and FcγRIIB.
source: 232T-expressing B cells lose the ability to inhibit the oligomerization of B cell receptors (BCRs) upon co-ligation between BCR and FcγRIIB (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: B cells expressing 232T fail to inhibit the spatial-temporal co-localization of BCR and CD19 within the B cell immunological synapses.
source: Recent live-cell imaging studies showed that B cells expressing 232T fail to inhibit the spatial-temporal co-localization of BCR and CD19 within the B cell immunological synapses (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Human primary B cells from SLE patients with homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T reveal hyper-activation of PI3K.

claim: There is a strong positive association of the homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism with SLE (χ2 = 27.224, p=0.008, odds ratio with 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.927).

claim: The homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism is significantly associated with early disease onset (age at disease onset <37, p=0.002).

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by clinical data analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism is significantly associated with elevation in the amounts of anti-dsDNA antibodies (p=0.004).

claim: I232T substitution enforces the inclination of the TM domain.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The inclination of the TM domain by I232T might result from the ability of H-bond formation between the side-chain Oγ atom of T232 and the backbone oxygen atom of a neighbor residue V228.
source: This inclination might result from the ability of H-bond formation between the side-chain Oγ atom of T232 and the backbone oxygen atom of a neighbor residue V228 (Figure 1B, left).

claim: The length between S218 and P221 peaks at 11 Å for 232T, about 3 Å longer than that for 232I.
source: And the length between S218 and P221 peaks at 11 Å for 232T, about 3 Å longer than that for 232I (Figure 1C).

claim: The main chain dihedral angle of P217 in 232I displays two populations at 141°±23° and −50°±12°.
source: The main chain dihedral angle of P217 in 232I displays two populations at 141°±23° and −50°±12°, respectively, but shifts to −40°±45° and −75°±12° in 232T (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The main chain dihedral angle of P217 in 232T shifts to −40°±45° and −75°±12°.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The ectodomain of 232I maintains more straight-up conformation, whereas that of 232T bends down toward the lipid bilayer.
source: The ectodomain of 232I maintains more straight-up conformation, whereas that of 232T bends down toward the lipid bilayer (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The ectodomain inclination angle of 232T distributes across 30 ~ 60° with a sharper single-peak at 40°.
source: Statistical analyses show that the ectodomain inclination angle of 232T distributes across 30 ~ 60° with a sharper single-peak at 40° (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The ectodomain inclination angle of 232I distributes much flatter with a favorable probability ranging from 50° to 70°.
source: In contrast, the angle of 232I distributes much flatter with a favorable probability ranging from 50° to 70° (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The distance of C1 domain to the membrane is shorter for 232T than 232I.
source: The distance of C1 domain to the membrane is shorter for 232T than 232I (Figure 1E).

claim: The tilting orientation of 232T may sterically prevent the accessibility of the IgG's Fc portion.
source: First, the tilting orientation of 232T may sterically prevent the accessibility of the IgG's Fc portion, as significant clashes between docked Fc and the membrane are observed, although FcγRIIB's Fc binding site is not completely buried into the membrane (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ectodomain of 232T is less flexible such that the chance for FcγRIIB to associate with the ligand is greatly decreased.

claim: I232T polymorphic change enhances the FRET efficiency about two folds, from ~20% in 232I to ~40% in 232T.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by FRET assay data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The enhancement of FRET efficiency by I232T polymorphism indicates that 232T ectodomain prefers to a more recumbent orientation on the plasma membrane than 232I.
source: This enhancement of FRET efficiency by I232T polymorphism indicates that 232T ectodomain prefers to a more recumbent orientation on the plasma membrane than 232I, consistent with above MDS observations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and inferred from FRET assay data.

claim: The in situ 2D effective binding affinity of 232I with human IgG1 antibody (anti-S) is about three times higher than that of 232T (AcKa = 3.03 ± 0.15×10−7 and 0.80 ± 0.04 × 10−7 μm4, respectively).
source: The results show that the in situ 2D effective binding affinity of 232I with human IgG1 antibody (anti-MERS virus S protein, or anti-S) is about three times higher than that of 232T (AcKa = 3.03 ± 0.15×10−7 and 0.80 ± 0.04 × 10−7 μm4, respectively), whereas that with human IgG4 is hardly measured as FcγRIIB and IgG4 binding is known to be extremely weak and beyond the detection limit (10−8 μm4) of this assay (Huang et al., 2010) (Figure 3B and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3B and F.

claim: The 2D off-rates of 232I and 232T from human IgG1 are similar (7.75 ± 1.42 and 7.62 ± 1.41 s−1, respectively).
source: Further analyses show that although the 2D off-rates of 232I and 232T from human IgG1 are similar (7.75 ± 1.42 and 7.62 ± 1.41 s−1, respectively) (Figure 3B and H), the 2D effective on-rate of 232T with IgG1 is three times slower than that of 232I (Figure 3B and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3B and H.

claim: The 2D effective on-rate of 232T with IgG1 is three times slower than that of 232I.
source: Further analyses show that although the 2D off-rates of 232I and 232T from human IgG1 are similar (7.75 ± 1.42 and 7.62 ± 1.41 s−1, respectively) (Figure 3B and H), the 2D effective on-rate of 232T with IgG1 is three times slower than that of 232I (Figure 3B and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3B and G.

claim: Both 2D effective affinity and on-rate of 232I with anti-gp120 human IgG1 are three times higher than those of 232T (AcKa = 7.74 ± 0.24×10−7 and 2.43 ± 0.11 × 10−7 μm4, respectively; Ackon=5.95±0.19 and 2.16 ± 0.10 × 10−7 μm4 s−1, respectively).
source: These results are also confirmed by using another human IgG1 antibody (anti-HIV1 gp120 IgG1, or anti-gp120). Both 2D effective affinity and on-rate of 232I with anti-gp120 human IgG1 are three times higher than those of 232T (AcKa = 7.74 ± 0.24×10−7 and 2.43 ± 0.11 × 10−7 μm4, respectively; Ackon=5.95±0.19 and 2.16 ± 0.10 × 10−7 μm4 s−1, respectively), while the respective off-rates are similar (7.70 ± 0.83 and 8.90 ± 1.61 s−1, respectively) (Figure 3C and F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3C and F–H.

claim: The off-rates of 232I and 232T with anti-gp120 human IgG1 are similar (7.70 ± 0.83 and 8.90 ± 1.61 s−1, respectively).

Both 2D effective affinity and on-rate of 232I with anti-gp120 human IgG1 are three times higher than those of 232T (AcKa = 7.74 ± 0.24×10−7 and 2.43 ± 0.11 × 10−7 μm4, respectively; Ackon=5.95±0.19 and 2.16 ± 0.10 × 10−7 μm4 s−1, respectively), while the respective off-rates are similar (7.70 ± 0.83 and 8.90 ± 1.61 s−1, respectively) (Figure 3C and F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3C and F–H.

claim: Fixing B cells expressing FcγRIIB by paraformaldehyde (PFA) does not alter the ligand binding defects for I232T polymorphic change.
source: We find that fixing B cells expressing FcγRIIB by paraformaldehyde (PFA) does not alter the ligand binding defects for I232T polymorphic change (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), suggesting the reduction of lateral diffusion by I232T hardly contributes to the reduction of the ligand binding affinity and on-rate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data on fixed cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduction of lateral diffusion by I232T hardly contributes to the reduction of the ligand binding affinity and on-rate.

claim: Homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T confers dramatically increased risk of developing more severe clinical manifestations in patients with SLE.
source: In summary, we confirm that homozygous FcγRIIB-I232T confers dramatically increased risk of developing more severe clinical manifestations in patients with SLE.

claim: The pathological relevance of I232T is caused by the inclination of the TM domain which leads to FcγRIIB ectodomain bending toward plasma membrane, significantly impairing FcγRIIB's binding ability to IgG's Fc portion through reducing in situ binding affinity and association rate.
source: The pathological relevant of I232T is caused by the inclination of the TM domain which leads to FcγRIIB ectodomain bending toward plasma membrane, significantly impairing FcγRIIB's binding ability to IgG's Fc portion through reducing in situ binding affinity and association rate.
evidence: This is stated in the summary and supported by molecular dynamics simulations, FRET assay, and adhesion frequency assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The hampered Fc recognition ability of FcγRIIB-I232T results in the deficiency on its inhibitory function and thus hyper-activated immune cells, potentially contributing to SLE.
source: The hampered Fc recognition ability of FcγRIIB-I232T results in the deficiency on its inhibitory function and thus hyper-activated immune cells, potentially contributing to SLE.

claim: The TM helix tilting and S218-P221 prolongation for 232T can be readily observed in lipid membranes with different-length lipids.
source: The TM helix tilting and S218-P221 prolongation for 232T can be readily observed in these two systems (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–4C.

claim: FcγRIIB's Fc binding site is not completely buried into the membrane in 232T.
source: First, the tilting orientation of 232T may sterically prevent the accessibility of the IgG's Fc portion, as significant clashes between docked Fc and the membrane are observed, although FcγRIIB's Fc binding site is not completely buried into the membrane (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Significant clashes between docked Fc and the membrane are observed for 232T.
source: First, the tilting orientation of 232T may sterically prevent the accessibility of the IgG's Fc portion, as significant clashes between docked Fc and the membrane are observed, although FcγRIIB's Fc binding site is not completely buried into the membrane (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: FcγRIIB and IgG4 binding is extremely weak and beyond the detection limit (10−8 μm4) of the adhesion frequency assay.
source: The results show that the in situ 2D effective binding affinity of 232I with human IgG1 antibody (anti-MERS virus S protein, or anti-S) is about three times higher than that of 232T (AcKa = 3.03 ± 0.15×10−7 and 0.80 ± 0.04 × 10−7 μm4, respectively), whereas that with human IgG4 is hardly measured as FcγRIIB and IgG4 binding is known to be extremely weak and beyond the detection limit (10−8 μm4) of this assay (Huang et al., 2010) (Figure 3B and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The lateral diffusion has negligible impact on 2D affinity of receptor-ligand binding on live cells.
source: Moreover, Zhu and colleagues have also extensively discussed and experimentally proved that the lateral diffusion has negligible impact on 2D affinity of receptor-ligand binding on live cells (Chesla et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The FcγRIIIA-F158V polymorphism is a binding-enhancing polymorphism.
source: To further exclude potential technical artifacts in in situ single-cell adhesion frequency assay, we confirm previously known binding-enhancing FcγRIIIA-F158V polymorphism by using the 2D binding assay in this report (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: I232T polymorphic change in the TM domain of FcγRIIB allosterically tilts FcγRIIB ectodomains toward the plasma membrane, rendering steric hindrance of its ligand binding domain.
source: All these data strongly support that I232T polymorphic change in the TM domain of FcγRIIB allosterically tilts FcγRIIB ectodomains toward the plasma membrane, rendering steric hindrance of its ligand binding domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations, FRET assay, and adhesion frequency assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: 232T exhibits significantly reduced 2D affinity and association on-rate to IgG antibodies.
source: As a result, 232T exhibits significantly reduced 2D affinity and association on-rate to IgG antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by adhesion frequency assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Similar allosteric regulation may be applied to a broad range of transmembrane receptors.
source: To be noted, it is possible that similar allosteric regulation may be applied to a broad range of transmembrane receptors, for example, potentially explaining how membrane anchor pattern of CD16a influences ligand recognition (Chesla et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and represents a speculative statement about broader implications.

claim: The membrane anchor pattern of CD16a influences ligand recognition.
source: To be noted, it is possible that similar allosteric regulation may be applied to a broad range of transmembrane receptors, for example, potentially explaining how membrane anchor pattern of CD16a influences ligand recognition (Chesla et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: FcγRIIB-I232T is the first example that a naturally occurring diseases-associated SNP within the TM domain of a single-pass transmembrane receptor can allosterically suppress the receptor's ligand recognition and signaling functions.
source: Thus, it is very likely that FcγRIIB-I232T is the first example that a naturally occurring diseases-associated SNP within the TM domain of a single-pass transmembrane receptor can allosterically suppress the receptor's ligand recognition and signaling functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: FcγRIIB's suppressive function is triggered by its ligand engagement.
source: FcγRIIB's suppressive function is triggered by its ligand engagement, while this function is disrupted by a single amino acid change in the 232th residue from Ile to Thr in FcγRIIB's TM domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about FcγRIIB function.

claim: The suppressive function of FcγRIIB is disrupted by a single amino acid change in the 232th residue from Ile to Thr in FcγRIIB's TM domain.
source: FcγRIIB's suppressive function is triggered by its ligand engagement, while this function is disrupted by a single amino acid change in the 232th residue from Ile to Thr in FcγRIIB's TM domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Two early biochemical studies proposed a model of reduced affinity between 232T and lipid rafts to explain the functional relevance and effect of this natural mutation.
source: Two early biochemical studies proposed a model of reduced affinity between 232T and lipid rafts to explain the functional relevance and effect of this natural mutation (Floto et al., 2005; Kono et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: A recent study proposed a model that I232T mutation enforces the inclination of the TM domain inside the membrane, thereby reducing the lateral mobility and inhibitory functions of FcγRIIB.
source: A recent study also proposed a different model that I232T mutation enforces the inclination of the TM domain inside the membrane, thereby reducing the lateral mobility and inhibitory functions of FcγRIIB (Xu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Both previous models assumed that 232T and FcγRIIB-WT (232I) have an equal capability to perceive and bind to their ligands.
source: However, both models assumed that 232T and FcγRIIB-WT (232I) have an equal capability to perceive and bind to their ligands, the IgG's Fc portion within the antibody-antigen immune complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a critique of previous models.

claim: The assumption that 232T and 232I have equal ligand binding capability is based on the argument that they are identical in the amino acid sequence of their extracellular domains.
source: This important but experimentally un-proved pre-requisition in both models is based on the argument that 232T and 232I are identical in the amino acid sequence of their extracellular domains and thus the potential structure of ligand binding site for recognizing the ligands, that is, the IgG's Fc portions (Dal Porto et al., 2004; D'Ambrosio et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: There is no direct experimental evidence to validate the assumption that 232T and 232I have equal ligand binding capability.
source: However, to date, there is no direct experimental evidence to validate this pre-requisite assumption.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a gap in the literature that the study addresses.

claim: The membrane buried non-helical region of the linker extends more in 232T than that in 232I.
source: The membrane buried non-helical region of the linker extends more in 232T than that in 232I.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The SNP I232T occurs at a notable frequency in up to 40% (heterozygous polymorphism) humans.
source: These clinical association analyses demonstrate that SLE patients homozygous for FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism are prone to develop more severe clinical manifestations than the patients carrying heterozygous FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism or FcγRIIB-WT, reinforcing the importance to study the pathogenic mechanism of FcγRIIB-I232T polymorphism since this SNP occurs at a notable frequency in up to 40% (heterozygous polymorphism) humans (Niederer et al., 2010; Smith and Clatworthy, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations.
